lots.what_it_is: Three table forks and a table spoon, fiddle and thread pattern, German 800 silver (crescent moon and crown mark with 800, plus a maker's mark), retailer or maker name POCHON. Catalogued at 191g.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Leopard Antiques $390 pair of forks (page opened: pair of ornate baluster handled two-prong Paris 800 forks with steel tines, 82g, price shown only as $; a different form and decoration with steel tines, not comparable to plain one-piece fiddle and thread table forks; at most a loose category guide, and an asking price). The goldpricez silver spot is a melt reference only, not an entry. My own new searches could not run (session web search limit reached), so no auction comparables were added.
lots.guide_summary: No surviving sold, unsold or asking entries for comparable 800 cutlery. Melt reference only: 191g x 0.800 = 152.8g fine silver x A$2.74/g (goldpricez, page opened, 8 Oct 2026 AEDT) = about A$419 at full spot; a scrap buyer typically pays less, perhaps 80 to 90% of spot (about A$335 to A$375), which is an estimate, not a seen price.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so both maximum bids are 0 under the rules. For information only: melt at full spot about A$419; if a scrap or bullion buyer paid about 85% of spot (about A$356), the break-even hammer for melting would be about A$356 / 1.198 = A$297, and a 2x-margin melt flip would be about A$356 / 2.396 = A$148. These depend on the 191g weight being right and are not SOLD-backed.
lots.confidence_reason: Marks read clearly in the photos, but no SOLD or UNSOLD comparables, and value rests on melt reasoning and an unverified catalogue weight.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 enlarged: crescent moon, crown, '800' and a third round maker's mark, then 'POCHON'. The crescent and crown with 800 is the German national silver mark (used from 1888), not French or Belgian as the researcher guessed. POCHON may be a retailer (a Bern jeweller of that name is known, but I could not verify it). Photo 1 enlarged: forks are one-piece with silver tines, not steel-tined, so nearly all the weight should be silver. Light wear and tarnish, normal use.
lots.condition: Good used condition: light surface scratches and tarnish, tines straight, no visible damage or repairs.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the 191g weight on scales, and that all four pieces carry the 800 and crescent and crown marks?
